method: Six manually identified architecture correspondences fitted by unrobust projective least squares; no boundary vertices, cursor, gate symbols, zone badges, text or icons used for fitting. Three architecture and five border checks are withheld from the fit. An additional attempted architecture check H4 was visually rejected because it lies on a plain pavement edge rather than an identifiable corner; it remains in the receipt and review panel but is excluded from accuracy summaries. Initial point roles were fixed before fitting; neither the fitted controls nor transform changed after review. All observations and first-pass picks are retained.

points.label: REJECTED plain west pavement edge
points.rejection: The labelled crop showed a straight pavement edge, not an independently identifiable corner. Retained transparently; excluded from holdout statistics despite its low residual.

points.label: south gate west outer shoulder
points.correction: The first pick was inside the symbol apron. A 12x nearest-neighbour native crop showed the external green-line shoulder at x1135. No fit point, role or transform was changed; both residuals are retained.

points.label: south gate east outer shoulder
points.correction: The 12x native inspection locates the external green-line shoulder one pixel west of the first pick. No fit point, role or transform was changed; both residuals are retained.

West gate symbol covers the inner crossing. The source exposes both shoulders; their connection is unreviewed. This is not a traversable entrance claim.

occlusions: The native red cursor overlaps the west perimeter and southwest corner; use the original closeup and two retained PR200 images for those spans.
The native crown and zone badge obscure the north gate region/interior; original photo identity and surrounding architecture are used, never the crown/badge geometry.
The closeup's cursor, place name and badge lie inside the zone and are not used as landmarks or polygon edges.
Gate symbols cover short crossing spans in every supplied view. These three connectors remain explicit candidate interpretations, not newly observed geography.
